title: ReadCode: try finding problems in code you didn't write
consent: ReadCode is a practice tool for the interview rounds where you read, debug or review code someone else wrote. We are testing an early version with people who are looking for a job, and want to know whether it is worth building. It takes about an hour.
You will work through five tasks on a small payments API and a food-delivery backend, from a warm-up to a hard one. The last one is optional in spirit: do your best and move on if you are stuck.

We record your answers, how long each task takes, and the questions you answer before and after. We do not record your name or email with your answers; your participant code is the only link. You can stop at any time, and ask us to delete your answers using your code.
Please do not use AI assistants or web search during the tasks. At the end we ask whether you did; answering honestly does not affect anything.

survey.label: Are you looking for a software engineering job right now?
Years working as a software engineer (not counting internships)
How comfortable are you reading Python? (1 = barely, 5 = daily)
In the last 12 months, did an interview ask you to read, explain, debug or review code you didn't write?
If yes: which company or companies, and what did the round look like? (optional)
What do you mostly use to prepare for interviews?

end_intro: Honest answers help us most, including "not useful". None of this affects you.

honesty.label: How would you feel if you could no longer use ReadCode?
Would you use ReadCode to prepare for your next interview?
Did the tasks feel like real engineering work?
How hard were the tasks overall?
What is the main thing you got out of it? (optional)
Did you use an AI assistant (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot...) during any task?
Did you search the web for any task?
Anything that was confusing or felt unfair? (optional)
